findings.reason: Confirmed. The roadmap's ContDiffOn predicate requires finite right derivatives of every order at zero; an arbitrary finite Laplace measure does not supply them. For the probability measure sum_{n>=1} 2^(-n) delta_(2^n), the nonnegative right difference quotient (1-f(t))/t dominates every finite partial sum, whose limit is N. Hence the right derivative is not finite. Also exp(-n t) tends on the closed half-line to the discontinuous indicator of zero. The pin's HausdorffBernsteinWidder.lean:70 proves the finite-measure iff for IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi, not the stronger IsCompletelyMonotone. Representation.lean:504 gives the all-moments strong converse. Use the weaker predicate for the iff and keep the strong within-derivative predicate separate. Limits.lean:68 and :96 already provide open-half-line pointwise-limit closure and the endpoint-continuous version. Endpoint continuity repairs closure of the weaker class only: partial sums of the first counterexample give a continuous limit that is still not endpoint-smooth. Correct the prose and displayed stub, import these existing theorems, and preserve the reviewed qualified library credit.

Confirmed. A=I on the real Banach space R has resolvent (lambda-1)^(-1) I and the advertised power bounds with M=1, omega=1, but its unshifted Yosida approximation is lambda/(lambda-1) I. Its positive-time exponential has norm greater than one. Thus the common contraction sentence is false in the general-growth regime. Engel–Nagel II.3.5 proves the contraction case; II.3.8 first shifts and uses an equivalent norm for general M. The pin instead supplies the direct exponent-zero M-bound at HilleYosida/Approximation.lean:105, the shift at Shift.lean:49, and the completed shifted-limit construction/generation theorem at Generation.lean:165–205. Import the existing real-Banach-space generation result, with its density, M>=1 and all-resolvent-powers hypotheses; its Lean HasGrowthBound argument order is omega M. Keep the contraction route under dissipativity/range hypotheses and do not assert that shifting alone makes the original-norm bound contractive when M>1. No new semigroup implementation or owner is needed.

Confirmed. On the additive monoid of nonnegative reals with identity involution, F(t)=exp(t) has quadratic form |sum_i c_i exp(t_i)|^2, so it satisfies exactly the generic PD definition. It is continuous at zero but exceeds F(0)=1 and is not uniformly continuous: at n and n+exp(-n) its values differ by a quantity tending to one. PositiveDefinite/Basic.lean:206 retains the general diagonal Cauchy-Schwarz bound; :213 requires a+star(a)=0 for the bound by F(0). Continuity.lean:250 assumes a seminormed additive group and globally negating involution. Apply those qualifications explicitly. Preserve the generic monoid definition and BCR's separately stated boundedness hypothesis; the BCR representation theorem is not refuted by this unbounded example. Keep the reviewed library credit, which already records the restrictions.

Confirmed. The August 17, 2010 draft's Definition 3.2 uses dimension <d-1, whereas the December 10 revision uses <=d-1; Proposition 3.5 proves uniqueness under the revised predicate. The native roadmap still uses the old strict threshold. In R^2, uniform probability laws on perpendicular centered unit-half-length segments vanish on all Borel sets of dimension <1. Every coupling has squared cost 2/3, and equal/opposite parameter couplings give distinct diagonal midpoint laws. Both achieve 1/6 for the averaged squared-distance objective, its triangle-inequality lower bound, so uniqueness fails. Replace the threshold by <=n-1, cite the revised definition/proposition and retain probability, finite-second-moment and positive normalized weight hypotheses. One qualifying input suffices for uniqueness; the simultaneous Brenier-map characterization of Proposition 3.8 assumes the condition on every input. Keep absolute continuity and bounded-density estimates separate. This corrects an obsolete manuscript condition rather than reporting a new error in the revised source. The barycenter target remains unbuilt.

Confirmed. A Mobius preimage of the real axis is a generalized circle. The regular analytic parabola t+i t^2 lies on no line or circle on an interval: substitution in a generalized-circle equation forces its quadratic-in-modulus coefficient, both linear coefficients and constant to vanish. It cannot be straightened by a Mobius map. The local inverse of h(z)=z+i z^2, with h'(0)=1, does give a biholomorphic straightening chart. The pin's Reflection/Arc.lean:160 already proves charted reflection for holomorphic open partial homeomorphisms, conjugation-invariant coordinate domains, correct mapping conditions, continuity on the closed side, holomorphy on the open side and the real-boundary condition. Restrict Mobius reduction to lines/circles and import that chart theorem for regular analytic arcs. Preserve all source and target chart hypotheses and the existing built verdict; no new reflection theory is needed.
